newsitem.title: UK: UK union says to consider BA proposals.
newsitem.headline: UK union says to consider BA proposals.

text.p: The main union involved in an industrial dispute between British Airways Plc Plc and its cabin crew over pay said on Thursday it would consider BA's proposals aimed at resolving the conflict which have been sent to the arbitration service ACAS.
"We have received proposals from the company which we are considering," Bill Morris, general secretary of the Transport and General Workers Union, said in a statement.
"We regret that we are not having direct negotiations with British Airways which would facilitate a speedy response."
The T&G's Morris, who is leading the unions in a bitter face-off with BA chief executive Robert Ayling over pay and conditions, repeated that he wanted talks to start as soon as possible.
"We are convening a meeting of our cabin crew representatives to consider the proposals submitted by BA through ACAS," he said.
The BA conflict is the first threat of major industrial action under the new Labour government.

British Airways said earlier it had sent a proposal to the arbitration service to try to settle the dispute as a strike deadline neared. BA cabin crew have threatened a three-day strike next week over plans to restructure pay and conditions, which are part of its goal of saving one billion pounds by the end of the century.
Officials from the Transport & General Workers Unions say the package would cut cabin crew salaries and have objected to BA sealing a deal with the smaller Cabin Crew 89 union.

A BA spokesman said the airline's proposal addressed two main concerns -- the union's fears about its members being worse off under the new arrangement, and the relationships between the two cabin crew unions.

BA is involved in a separate dispute with ground staff over the sell-off of its catering division. Ground staff union representatives are still meeting to decide what action to take, despite BA's offer of talks to resolve the disagreement.
BA shares were down 9-1/2p at 681-1/2 at 1525 GMT in a strong UK market.
